svg.title: RIEMANN F2 — What is new: the 200 statements new in Alpöge's proof, where they sit, how they lean on each other, and what they take from the literature
svg.desc: Every other poster colours provenance; this one is organised by it. The blueprint marks each statement new in Alpöge's proof (200), modified from a published result (61), or published as it stands (142); 13 carry no mark. The new statements are too many for a card each: their own graph has 263 proof-use edges and chains 16 statements long. So this poster works one level up. Each chapter is a card holding only its new work: its sections with how much of each is new, the new statements that nothing new builds on, and what its new work takes and gives. An arrow from A to B, labelled with a count, says that the proofs of B's new statements use that many new statements of A; read it from the foot up, as diagram R2. The matrix below the cards has every such count, the arrows that would point upward included. Then every section by provenance, which is where the new work concentrates; the published and modified results the new statements lean on most; and the new lemmas that published results' proofs use. No Lean was built: see diagram R1, band 5.
svg.text: RIEMANN · F2

text.tspan: How to read a chapter card

svg.text: A chapter card holds only the chapter's new work. The pill counts it against the chapter's statements. The bullets are the chapter's sections, each with its statements by provenance, so a section that is all new reads 9 of 9 new.

Tops are the new statements of the chapter that no new statement uses, in its statement or its proof: the chapter's new work ends there, in a theorem the outline uses, or in a lemma a published result's proof uses (band 6). On the literature alone counts the new statements that use no new statement: the new work
begins there.

Takes and gives are the proof uses between new statements across chapters, the arrows' counts; inputs are the published, modified and unlabelled statements the chapter's new work uses, with the most used named.
Rows: the chapters stand as on diagram R2, used above user, so most arrows point down. The 5 pairs that point up are not drawn as arrows: they are listed beside the cards and counted in the matrix.
200 new statements in 9 chapters: 91 theorems, 62 lemmas, 32 propositions, 14 definitions, 1 corollarys.
263 proof uses between new statements, 314 uses with stated-with counted; 61 of the proof uses cross a chapter, in 16 ordered pairs of chapters.
16 tops: new statements nothing new builds on. 65 on the literature alone: new statements that use nothing new.
1345 uses of 202 inputs: 59 modified, 135 published, 8 unlabelled results.
34 uses of 24 new statements by statements that are not new: new lemmas inside published results (band 6).
199 of the 200 name a Lean declaration; 599 declarations in all.
Published results at the top, the five stages in the middle, the outline and the main theorems at the foot, as on diagram R2. The arrows count proof uses between new statements across chapters.

text.tspan: What the stages pass to each other

svg.text: The three interface definitions of the outline, local parameters, polarised Galois representations and the Tate–Shafarevich bound, are what the new work of the arithmetic stages hands to the analytic ones;
diagram F1 draws them. Only the Tate–Shafarevich bound is itself new; the other two are modified from the literature, so they count as inputs here.

The 24 new statements whose users include a statement that is not new: the proof of a published or modified result, as the blueprint gives it, leans on them. They are where the new work reaches into the literature chapter rather than the other way round.
